transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-06 15:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jesse Huang (Redwood Solutions), Maya Rodriguez (BrightScale, Head of ML), Ethan Cole (BrightScale, SRE), Priya Singh (BrightScale, Product), Alex Kim (BrightScale, Data Eng)

Summary (auto): Demo focused on migration parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API and console, and pilot/benchmark planning.

00:00 Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we are gonna run through a migration-oriented demo today, focus on parity mapping from openai/anthropic/together and show how it maps to the redwood api and console, also samir will run through optimize and batching suggestions
00:18 Maya (BrightScale): awesome thanks lena, quick note we have some HIPAA constraints so want to understand private deployment options and kms for key management
00:32 Lena: yep, we'll cover private/vpc and kms, samir do you want to kick off with the api parity mapping
00:40 Samir (Redwood SE): sure, thanks. so first thing is chat parity — openai style chat messages map to redwood's chat endpoint, same roles system user/assistant/system. function-calling is supported, we try to keep the same shape but we name a few fields slightly differently so we provide a mapping sheet, i'll show that now
01:05 Samir: note, some transcriptions may show "KV cash" but it's KV cache, we optimize the cache handling — sorry for the verbal slip
01:20 Jesse (Redwood): i'm gonna pull up the parity spreadsheet link here - https://app.redwood.ai/parity/brightscale-parity-spreadsheet (shared)
01:31 Ethan (BrightScale): link received, nice. on the functions part, how do you handle callbacks for tools? anthro- anthropic had a callback pattern we used, and together has a streaming plus callback blend
01:49 Samir: good question. redwood supports streaming tokens out of the box, and function/tool calling is done via the same chat route; we return a structured function call object, and you can optionally request async callback webhooks for long-running tools — we cover both patterns in the doc
02:12 Priya (BrightScale): does the SDK keep the same patterns as openai? like streaming event types and chunked responses? we have product features built on streaming partial replies
02:28 Samir: yes, the SDK mirrors common openai patterns. streaming events are chunked with delta tokens, we also support grpc streaming for lower overhead in dedicated/private deployments
02:46 Maya: GRPC is interesting — does that mean less latency for on-prem? we saw throughput issues with openai when doing heavy prompt loads
02:55 Samir: grpc lowers overhead, and with dedicated gpu pools you can get predictable tail latency, also batching and cache strategies matter — redwood optimize suggests batching configs per route automatically
03:12 Lena: quick case note, BrightScale mentioned they use both openai and anthropic in prod, sometimes together for redundancy — curious about model routing and fallback support
03:27 Samir: model routing is policy-driven, you can route by latency, cost, region, or explicit allowlist, and we support automatic fallback to quantized variants when full capacity isn't available
03:45 Alex (BrightScale): any gotchas around tokenization differences? we use some custom tokenizer handling for embeddings in our pipeline
03:58 Samir: tokenization can vary, embeddings can be slightly different across models; for migration we recommend running a small calibration set, we provide embedding similarity metrics and tools in the console to compare OpenAI embeddings vs Redwood-hosted model embeddings
04:18 Maya: that'd be great — we need to ensure retrieval quality doesn't drop, regen rate is tolerant up to 3% but anything more triggers product alerts
04:30 Jesse: on the console side i'll demo model pinning, rollout and the optimize suggestions — pull up the console now
04:40 Jesse: (screen share) here is the console route view, you can see per-route latency and cost, token breakdown, and per-token caller attribution for auditing. you can pin a route to a specific model version and create canaries
05:02 Ethan: how are audit logs exposed? we need immutable logs for compliance
05:12 Jesse: we surface audit logs via the console, and you can configure log export to s3 or syslog; for private deployments you can point to your own logging collector, logs are immutable with timestamped entries
05:29 Priya: what about sso and role based access? we need fine grained permissions for developers vs product vs security
05:38 Lena: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role based access controls, also partners can integrate with your idp for mfa enforcement
05:52 Maya: okay good. on encryption — we need customer-managed keys (hsm/kms) for at-rest and in-transit crypto, with key rotation
06:03 Samir: yes, we support cloud KMS integrations and bring-your-own-kms for private, and provide guidance for hsm if needed. we'll share architecture doc with key management patterns
06:18 Alex: network topology — do we need egress to public endpoints for telemetry? historic org policy is zero egress except to approved buckets
06:29 Jesse: for hosted you can opt out of telemetry, for private we let you host the control plane or keep logs local, we'll work with you on allowed egress rules
06:40 Maya: switching gears — let's do a quick demo of a migration snippet, show how we'd change an openai chat call to redwood
06:48 Samir: sure, here's an openai example (pseudo): openai.chat.completions.create({model: 'gpt-...', messages: [...]}) -> redwood.chat.create({model: 'redwood/gpt-xt', input: [...]}) we also provide 1:1 snippet conversions in the parity sheet
07:10 Samir: small gotcha: response field names vary, e.g., openai uses choices[0].message, redwood returns a top-level responses array; we give wrapper helpers in the sdk to normalize
07:29 Priya: will that require big code churn? our product layer expects openai response shapes in a few places
07:38 Samir: minimal churn if you use the sdk normalization layer; otherwise we provide a light compatibility shim that maps fields at the client side
07:49 Maya: how about rate limits and quotas, we have bursts during nightly jobs and also steady user loads
07:58 Lena: we expose quotas and burst policies, dedicated capacity gives predictable throughput and you can configure burst windows, and we also do automatic fallback to cheaper quantized models if you're close to quota
08:12 Alex: curious about cost delta — we use together for cheaper batch generation and openai for quality, how does pricing compare
08:22 Lena: we'll send a tailored pricing deck; generally dedicated gives unit cost improvements for heavy workloads and optimize auto-batching reduces per-token costs, we'll include cost modeling for your workload in the parity sheet
08:36 Maya: demo time — can you show optimize suggestions for batching and quantization
08:44 Jesse: (screen) optimize tab, here's recommended batch_size per route, suggested quant profiles (int8/int4) with expected perf/cost tradeoffs, and quality regression thresholds you can set to trigger alerts
09:05 Ethan: would quantization affect latency or just quality? in our tests quant sometimes spiked tail latencies
09:16 Samir: quant mainly reduces memory and can improve throughput, but kernel selection matters; our compiler picks kernels to minimize latency impact, and we recommend running the bench with your prompt distribution to tune it
09:33 Maya: ok let's talk about pilot scope — we want a 2-week pilot with 10k calls/day and a 1k prompt calibration set, plus a security review
09:46 Lena: sounds good. initial scope: 2-week pilot, dedicated small capacity, run parallel traffic via routing, measure latency/cost/quality, and produce a migration playbook
09:58 Priya: who will manage the pilot execution? do you have a solutions engineer assigned
10:06 Lena: samir will be primary SE, jesse will help with console onboarding, and i'll coordinate contract/pricing and champion at redwood
10:19 Maya: great. can we do an in-person perf run or remote? we prefer remote but need reproducible scripts
10:28 Samir: we'll provide a bench harness and scripts (k6/wrk style) and can run remote with you; i'll run an initial 1k prompt test and share results
10:40 Ethan: for legal & procurement — we need contract language about data usage and retention, and a SOC2 report
10:50 Lena: we'll send standard SOC2 + DPA and are open to markup, also we'll include data retention configs in dedicated/private
11:02 Alex: one more question on embeddings — can we keep embeddings stable across model swaps? our vector db rebuild costs are huge
11:13 Samir: you can pin embedding models and run canaries, we also support a dual-write pattern for transition where you write both embeddings and allow a shadow index until similarity meets threshold
11:28 Priya: that dual-write pattern sounds ideal. ok last bit — timeline. if we sign pilot by next week can we start in two weeks
11:38 Lena: yes if procurement moves quick we can start pilot in two weeks, we'll target kickoff 2026-05-20 if contract is agreed by 2026-05-13
11:52 Maya: excellent. quick recap?
12:00 Lena: recap — we'll send parity spreadsheet and conversion snippets, run a perf bench (samir), share SOC2 and private deployment docs (jesse), customers to share prompts and network constraints, schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-05-20 pending contract. action items recorded in the doc.
12:22 Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the thoroughness
12:28 All: thanks, bye

Notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash" -> "KV cache", "anthro" -> "anthropic"), speaker labels are accurate but timestamps are approximate.
